utterances.text: I must interrupt you again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He's not accusing you. He's just mentioning it as a matter of fact, if I understood how he put it. He's not putting blame on that decision, that it was a wrong or a right decision. He says: In your wisdom you made that decision --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- without criticising you, but he's say what he sees as the consequences of that decision from his point of view.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And I'm saying what I see as the consequences of his decision. I don't want to get into a question of whether -- I don't believe I'm the accused here and I don't certainly feel as if I'm under accusation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Of course not. And he's not accusing you of anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: My skin is not that thin. What I am concerned about is the appearance of justice in a case of this nature and the appearance of justice is, in my submission, damaged when the Defence genuinely do not have the opportunity to cross-examine on evidence as significant as the Prosecution maintains this to be. That is all I think that it is reasonable for me to say. I don't think it would have been appropriate for me to take it any further with the witness, having spent three days in this court, seeing whether that witness was prepared to say anything at all. And having heard that witness say in terms - and I'm looking at page 397, line 19 - in relation to -- in answer to a question about Pal Krasniqi and Skender Kuci, I'm -- that's back at line 11 of that page, Mr. Rogers asked him: "Mr. Kabashi, I return to these two men, Pal Krasniqi and Skender Kuci, what can you tell the Trial Chamber, please, about what you saw or heard in relation to those men in Jabllanice in 1998?" A few lines further down, and I don't think I'm missing anything of substance, Mr. Rogers will tell you if I am, he says: "The perpetrator is today free, was never, never detained, never charged, and I am speaking specifically of the same subject matter as I have seen many things in my life. How can I trust that Prosecution that it has done the best thing?" Now, the only reason that I mention that is that many grounds have been speculated upon as to why this witness has chosen not to answer, has said that he cannot answer, and it's clear that one of his grounds is he feels that he has been abused, not by Mr. Rogers personally, not by even those involved in the case today, but by those who investigated it all those years ago. He feels that he has been made a victim by the Prosecution in this case. The only simple issue was whether as Defence counsel it was possible for us to persuade him to say anything because we are not the Prosecution. He sees us standing here as the Defence. Is he prepared to answer our questions either? The answer is no. There's no point in taking it further.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I just raise one technical matter before Your Honours rise to consider this. During the course of your ruling you referred upon and relied on paragraph 16 of the Milosevic decision and turning to the operative paragraph, one passage that I don't think found voice in Your Honours' ruling is this and if I can just read it into the record, this is again from paragraph 16: "Where the witness is present before the Court and orally attests to the accuracy of a statement, the evidence entered into the record cannot be considered to be exclusively written within the meaning of Rule 92 bis. The testimony of the witness constitutes a mixture of oral and written evidence." Now, that being the case, the record that Your Honours will have to consider when evaluating the testimony, if it remains in evidence, is not the transcript in Limaj but the evidence of this witness here and the transcript in Limaj or such portions of the transcript in Limaj as you consider to be genuinely probative and to outweigh the unfairness. It is mixed testimony, part written/part oral. And since, as the Milosevic Appeals Chamber pointed out, it requires the witness orally to attest to the accuracy of the material, Your Honours would need to find on the criminal standard of proof that this witness had attested to the accuracy of his answers in Limaj. The standard of proof must be beyond reasonable doubt, the burden must be on the Prosecution, as in all such matters. It follows that Your Honours are going to need to address the answers that this witness gave about the reliability of his Limaj testimony against the criminal standard of proof. That's the first thing. And as far as I've understood Mr. Harvey's submission and if I've understood it correctly, I adopt it, Mr. Rogers gave notice to all of us on Monday night that if he didn't get answers from satisfactorily continuing to lead the witness in chief he would be thinking of applying to have him cross-examined by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He wanted to consider.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, well in fact he indicated in the letter on Friday that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The letter is not before the court --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, it was sent to the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We don't want to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, it was sent to the Registry. Well, I can indicate to Your Honours that he indicated to the Defence that he would in all probability apply to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In all probability.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I'm not saying he's bound to. Why didn't he? The answer is he wouldn't have gotten the answers. He knows it just as we knew it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't know based upon a decision that we recently received precisely how the Chamber wishes to treat issues of joining, so I rise to join in Mr. Harvey's remarks, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith. In the interests of expeditiousness, I think it's going to be important that we follow the rules. An applicant will stand up and motivate an application, there will be a response, there will be a reply and we'll stop, unless there is an application to further argue because otherwise we just keep jumping up all the time and we're getting to an end.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Rogers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: It appears I am already guilty of jumping up immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: May I -- I don't want to prolong things unnecessarily, but there are a couple of things Mr. Emmerson raised in his submissions relating to the value of the Limaj testimony and he said I hadn't provided a list of the parts of that transcript that went to issues in this case. Your Honour, I can very readily, quickly identify most of the relevant parts, and it is not just about Pal Krasniqi and Skender Kuci. It goes to many other issues, including the leadership at the base -- at Jabllanice, to the continuity of events between April 1998 through into June, July, and later, and also other events that are occurring around the area. So it is not just -- this man did not just talk about Pal Krasniqi and Skender Kuci. He dealt with other victims and individuals, some who are named in the indictment and some who are not, and the relationships between them, what he observed relating to two of the accused, a little bit about Mr. Haradinaj, but it's not just about those two. I'm sure having looked at the transcript Your Honours will already readily have noticed that. That was one short point. I think Your Honours have already dealt with it, the argument really is about weight and my learned friends have tried with I think nimbleness of foot was what I suggested I had, tried to avoid -- not avoid, but work that very delicate balance between arguments of probative ands value and weight and actually this is all about weight and I think my learned friends recognise that to some extent but they suggest there is no weight, there is no probative value. Your Honours, we don't accept that. There is clear probative value in the testimony. I don't think I need to say anymore; that's all I wish to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we go on, I must apologise here. Because of the break we had a little earlier, I have become remiss of how long we have been sitting for now and I'm just concerned about how long we have been sitting now. I am concerned about the tapes and the interpreters and everybody. I see the stenographer is throwing up her arms in the air in exasperation. It should be an appropriate point of time from her point of view to take a break. I see she's nodding her agreement. It's not the normal time for a break ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just check one point with you, Mr. Emmerson. Did you say the Registry is in receipt of your letter?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said you would send it --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What I said was I had understood -- if I'm wrong then I will correct myself, but I had understood that Mr. Rogers' letter, sent on Monday at 6.49 p.m. in which he says: You should expect an application to treat the witness as adverse --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure, sure, I understand --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Had been copied to the Registry and I'm looking at the list of names and it may be that it was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: No, I can answer that since I wrote it and sent it. It's not copied to the Registry. It was a courtesy between myself and my learned friends to try to assist them in their preparations. I shall make sure it is more fulsome and perhaps more formal in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Rogers. Is -- I'm not sure now how to work out my time. Can we take a break and come back at quarter past 12.00 and when we come back we will go up to the end of the day. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We did get the message that you do want to stand, but before you do can I just say to the parties that we heard your arguments on the application. The Chamber will consider it and come back to you. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you very much. I do believe the next witness that is going to be called by the Prosecution is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Surely. Thank you very much. I do believe the next witness that is going to be called by the Prosecution is Mr. Stijovic. The Balaj Defence team filed an ex parte urgent motion, for which we have not yet received a decision, which directly impacts upon our potential cross-examination of this witness. As a result of that, we may -- I don't say we may. We are not in a position to necessarily cross-examine him in the event that such a need arises. But then again, I don't know how the Chamber's going to rule on our motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith, we take the point that the decision has not been rendered yet. Would it prejudice you terribly if the witness goes on and gives his evidence --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It would not, Your Honour, but I wanted to alert you to it before he came in to take the stand -- and for that I stood up and then made the submission at that point in time, it would come to you unexpectedly and I didn't want that to occur.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We are very grateful to you for that consideration. We will try to expedite the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Rogers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Two matters before Ms. Kravetz takes over to deal with Mr. Stijovic. The first one relates to Witness 75. Your Honours, he's warned for later this week -- scheduled for later this week, I slipped into my jurisdiction for a moment. He's scheduled for later this week, and we -- he's on our 92 ter application and that's been granted, but we had sought to withdraw him from that list prior to the rendering of the decision. I make an oral motion now to reschedule him now as a live witness, call him viva voce. It won't add any more time to the time we have already sought, but I thought I should notify and ask the Court if we can reschedule him in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, thanks. I remember seeing something to that effect. Do the parties have any comment to make on that? Mr. Emmerson? Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: None, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He's so rescheduled.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: The other relates to Witness 80 and I wonder if we may go briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Madam Registrar. Mr. Rogers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you. The next witness will be Zoran Stijovic, please, and my colleagues Ms. Kravetz and Mr. Menon will be dealing with that. I will leave court with Your Honour's permission and see you next time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may leave the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROGERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, while Mr. Rogers is leaving and before the witness comes in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: So we can try to make a tidy start to this, Your Honours ruled yesterday in a confidential decision that the next witness's 92 ter statement and the transcripts of all of his previous testimony in this trial, both examination-in-chief, cross-examination, and all the Judges' questions would be admitted into evidence. The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes. I was going to say on the condition that he confirms everything that is in there is accurate is what he would say again, giving testimony in court. There is an important matter regarding the statement, the 92 ter statement, which should be resolved before the witness comes into court so we don't end up going backwards and forwards with the witness here. And that is that the statement that was admitted and which the Prosecution applied to have admitted in the re-trial is one which has a number of redactions in it. That was as a result of a ruling made by the previous Trial Chamber. It was that redacted statement that the Prosecution applied to have admitted in this trial in their motion which Your Honours ruled on yesterday. And I just wanted to confirm that that is the statement - in other words the redacted statement with a number of paragraphs taken out - which will be the statement that the witness is asked to confirm and which will come into evidence. That's the first point. There's another point but perhaps that should be dealt with first before I move on to another one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may address that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: We have noted that same statement in our 92 ter application is listed in annex 1 so it is effectively the same, redacted, statement that was admitted in the previous trial. We're not seeking to tender the unredacted version of the statement and that had been notified to the Defence in the annex to our motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. The reason why I raised this was because on the Prosecution's notification of exhibits that they wished to use with this witness, the unredacted statement is on that list and I just wanted to make sure that they weren't going to try and use that statement with this witness when in fact the one that they had applied for was the redacted one which is the one that Your Honours ruled should be admitted. If that is now clear we needn't take that further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: The second matter, if I may, that is, there were a number of documents that were shown to this witness during his testimony which lasted some seven days. Many of those documents were not finally admitted by a ruling of the previous Trial Chamber, as we have indicated to Your Honours before. The Prosecution, as I understand it, only intends to put one of those documents - this is from the notification of exhibits - only one of those, and we'll deal with that document when it arises. But I do think it's important as that testimony as a body of evidence is being admitted that the ruling of the previous Trial Chamber is taken into account to this extent, which is that when those documents were excluded they ruled that the 92 ter statement could be admitted but to the extent that those documents had been excluded they weren't deleted or redacted from the 92 ter statement; they were left there. But the Trial Chamber found that what they would do is they would simply ignore those documents when they read that 92 ter statement and they would take the statements made in relation to those documents as being unsourced. So we do wish to stress that when that statement is read, the documents that are excluded and which the Prosecution hasn't sought to now reintroduce are not taken into account in accordance with the Trial Chamber's previous ruling because it's that statement that the Prosecution has applied to be admitted and has been admitted subject to those redactions and documents that are inadmissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Dixon, this Chamber has mentioned repeatedly that we really are not living in the shadow of the previous trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Number one. Number two, this Trial Chamber takes note of the caution that the Appeals Chamber made in its decision that the fact that certain things happened in the previous trial should be taken into account. However, we also take note of the fact that the same decision does say of the Appeals Chamber that it is quite possible to admit here what was not admitted there or not to admit here what was admitted there. It's all going to depend on whether whatever is being tendered passes the admissibility test as we all know it; and of course to the extent that the Appeals Chamber has flagged that caution, the Trial Chamber will take into account. But I do not think that this Trial Chamber is bound to take the same steps that were taken by the previous Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Exactly right. I only make the point to ensure that it is clear that the evidence that is now coming in was subject to certain removals, redactions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I suggest to you --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: -- by the prior Trial Chamber, which the Prosecution doesn't seem to be contesting in most cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I suggest, Mr. Dixon, that at the appropriate time when something comes in which you think shouldn't come in that you jump up and object and let's deal with the objection at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes, this was just to precurse that that might happen -- this is just the context --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure, but the way you are putting it, you are tying this Chamber's hands and tying the Prosecution's hands. I suggest that you object at the time when it's appropriate to object.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: There will be some objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That will come.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think that Mr. Dixon was trying to tie anybody's hands, but rather it should be viewed in slightly a different form, which is if the state of play remains the same and there has been a pre-existing ruling which one could call the law of the case or one could call guidance, if that is a situation in which we find ourselves in, then you are encouraged obviously to take into consideration and to follow the previous Trial Chamber's ruling. If that is not the case and the state of the play remains the same and you do not, then we run dangerously close to issues concerning double jeopardy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I should answer you, except just to say there is no question of double jeopardy. This is a re-trial --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- to the extent that these counts go as if on these six counts there was no trial at all. It's a re-trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yeah, I appreciate what you just said, but that still does not -- but that still does not unfortunately avoid the issue of double jeopardy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, but you --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand your position, Your Honour, and I understand what you've said, but by saying that this is a re-trial on these six counts does not in and of itself -- you can call it a de novo trial, you may call it what you will, it does not necessarily avoid underlying principles of double jeopardy. That's all I'm saying and I'm not taking it any further. I hope we don't reach that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I have no submissions to make on the point being raised by Mr. Guy-Smith at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's just that you are on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Oh, I'm just waiting for the witness to be brought in, Your Honour, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me say this, perhaps this is just an idiosyncrasy of mine. I'm used to -- when counsel stands up on the one side, other counsel sits. When you are both standing it is as if you are about to get into the ring literally and I can give you boxing gloves and we can hit the bell and you can box. I would request when one is talking, the other sits. So when you are standing I feel I have to come quickly to you to say what do you want to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I take the point, Your Honour. I heard the door and thought the witness was coming in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Okay. We are in open session. May the witness be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the witness please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good afternoon, sir. May you please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Could you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Zoran Stijovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When and where were you born, Mr. Stijovic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 13th of November, 1962, in Podgorica, in Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, have you previously provided a statement to the Office of the Prosecution of this Tribunal on 26 September 2007?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Have you recently had the opportunity to review that statement?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And having reviewed your statement, does it accurately reflect what you said at the time when you were interviewed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does. It reflects what I said at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And if you were examined today on the same issues, would you provide the same answers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I certainly would.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, the statement is 65 ter 00931 and I seek to tender it into evidence at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The statement is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit P121.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, have you previously testified before this Tribunal in the case of Haradinaj et al. in October of 2007?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did testify.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Have you over the past days had the opportunity to review the record of your prior testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have. Over the last weekend I reviewed or actually I listened to the audio recording of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And having reviewed the audio of the transcript, are you satisfied that it accurately reflects what you said at the time when you provided testimony in that case?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it reflects what I said at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And if examined on the same issues today, would you provide the same answers, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I certainly would basically. Perhaps there would be some terminological additions, but the answers to the same questions would be essentially the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender the transcript into evidence. There are two 65 ters. The first one is 04049, that's the public redacted version of the transcript. And the second one is 04050, and that version should be tendered under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If I might, Your Honour, before you make a ruling on that matter, may I voir dire the witness with one discreet issue concerning his audio review of the transcript of the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said may you do what?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Voir dire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. You may.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Good morning, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Good morning, sir, you indicated that you --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: -- listened to the audio of your testimony over the weekend. Could you tell us how many hours you spent listening to your audio of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, wouldn't that be relevant at cross-examination time, Mr. Guy-Smith?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, may be relevant now with regard to the admissibility of the information because it may go directly to his credibility; it may not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, I think that's a matter my learned colleague can address with the witness when it his turn comes to question him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what I'm trying to explore with counsel in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'll take it up later, if you will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I think it's more appropriate to deal with it now, but I'm in your hands as is said in these halls.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Let's do it at the time of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I ask that those two versions of the transcript be assigned exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, those two transcript -- 65 ter numbers are admitted into evidence. May you please give them an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 04049 will be Exhibit P122 and 65 ter 04050 will be Exhibit P123 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, there are a number of associated exhibits, exhibits that are associated to both the transcript and the written statement of this witness which have been listed in our -- in the annex to our 92 ter application. We have provided the court officer and also the Defence with the list of the exhibits that we consider to be associated to both the written statement and the transcript, and we seek that those be admitted into evidence. What I propose is that rather, since it's a very long list, as Your Honours are probably aware from our application, rather than reading each one of the 65 ters into the record, I would propose that Your Honours order the court officer at a later stage to assign exhibit numbers to those exhibits. But I'm in Your Honour's hands. If you prefer me to read -- to go through each 65 ter number and tender it, I can also proceed in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We can make that order only if there is no objection from the Defence. If there is, I'm afraid, we may have to deal with each one of them seriatim.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as the Haradinaj Defence is concerned, as we indicated in our response to the 92 ter motion there is no objection to those documents which were admitted in the original trial which this witness gave evidence about in examination-in-chief and in cross-examination. It's only those that were not admitted which are not on that list. So there's no objection to these all be giving numbers. The only condition is that the Prosecution has left off some of the exhibits that were shown to the witness. Providing those can be added so that when Your Honours read the transcript all the documents that were shown to the witness that were admitted are on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Shouldn't you rather tender them in your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: I think that can be done when we get on our feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did I understand you to say clearly it's on the list only those which were tendered in the previous trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: And admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And admitted. And cross-examined?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The others are not there?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: The others are not on that list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you have no objection to the entire list?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is a correct statement of the Balaj Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And of the Brahimaj Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then, all the annexes to the statement and transcripts may be admitted into evidence and may Madam Registrar at a time outside of court at her convenience give them exhibit numbers. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, an internal memorandum will be filed as soon as numbers have been assigned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Madam Registrar. Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, just one more issue in relation to the associated exhibits. I just wanted to bring to Your Honour's attention the fact that about 13 of these documents were admitted in the previous trial with draft English translations. We have kept the draft translations in the e-court system simply not to modify the record of what was admitted previously, but should Your Honours want to also benefit from having a revised translation into the e-court system that -- we can provide that and upload it at this stage -- and I'm just saying this because when the time comes for you to review the exhibits you may -- you will realise many of them say draft or unrevised and that's just how they were admitted in the previous case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me be clear I understand you. To the extent that translations are already in e-court, I do not think that the Trial Chamber would want a duplication. To the extent that you say you -- they are drafts or unrevised, to that extent I find it a little surprising that they are called drafts when they are already admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: They were admitted in the previous trial in that manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So I can't explain why that happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I presume there was just no time to obtain revised translations at the time, but this is just my guess.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. May --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I'm a bit surprised by the position the Prosecution takes. Exhibits were admitted, they're part of the record, they've relied on the record, they've made that part of their 92 ter statement, they are the associated exhibits set from the basis of this gentleman's testimony. The idea at this point or the notion that substituted translations of any sort would go in at this point in time we would object to. It is inappropriate for a plethora of reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: As I've just said to Madam Kravetz, we don't -- the Chamber doesn't find it necessary to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Anyway, let the record show that they are no longer drafts, but as -- as admitted into evidence now they are part of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That's fine. With Your Honour's leave I will proceed now to read a summary of this witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The witness worked as head of the analytical section of the Pristina centre of the Serbian State Security Service, RDB, between 1995 and 1999. He describes the area of responsibility of the Djakovica SUP. He also describes the sources through which the police collected information. The witness describes the organisation of the RDB in Kosovo and how the RDB and the analytical section received intelligence and information through three regional RDB centres: Pristina, Prizren, and Gnjilane centres. The witness describes the flow of information from an RDB operative in the field all the way up to Belgrade. He also describes the organisation and the role of the analytical section in Pristina. The witness describes the sources from which the analytical section received information. From the mid-1990s an operation called Krug, circle, was conducted by the RDB in Pristina to monitor the activities of the LPK and the KLA. The witness describes this operation. He also describes the development of the organisation of the KLA. He describes the role of Ramush Haradinaj in organising the KLA in the Dukagjin zone and the role of Lahi Brahimaj in Jablanica. The witness states that he received intelligence that Idriz Balaj, a.k.a., Toger was the commander of a KLA rapid-reaction unit called the Black Eagles which had its headquarters at a school in Rznic and that he was widely regarded as being under the direct command of Ramush Haradinaj. Finally, the witness speaks about KLA communiqués and indicates that they are consistent with information received by the SUP from other sources. That is the end of the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Stijovic, I would like to start by showing you a document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could please have 65 ter 03067 up on the screen. And if only the Serbian version could be displayed for the witness and we can have the English for the rest of the Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You have the document before you, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, could you -- do you recognise this document; and if yes, could you please comment on it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I do recognise the document. This is an official note from a working meeting held on the 26th of February, 1997, at the premises of the state security department centre in Prizren. This working meeting was attended by the head of the Kosovo and Metohija state security head, Mr. Gajic, co-ordinator of the 3rd administration of the KiM, Ljubomir Joksic, the then head of the CRDB Prizren, Milivoj Savic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you, can you speak a little bit slower. I see that the interpreter is struggling to keep pace with you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I apologise. The chief of the state security centre in Prizren, Mr. Milivoj Savic; his assistant, Jovanovic; head of the ORDB Pec, Mr. Branko Djukic; and head of the ORDB Djakovica, Sreten Camovic. The introduction at the meeting was given by the Djakovica state security department chief, Mr. Camovic, who informed those present about the information, about the existence of an illegal group in the village of Jablanica, in the municipality of Djakovica, headed by Lahi Brahimaj and about the measures which the Djakovica operative sector undertook in relation to that group, namely, previous processing of Lahi Brahimaj was recorded, previous processing is a form of work of the State Security Service, implying the review of all members of that group through Lahi Brahimaj and further planning of work and operation. In the conclusions of the meeting a series of specific activities was agreed upon which were to be initiated in the forthcoming period so that this indicated and identified hostile activity at the time by Mr. Lahi Brahimaj could be dealt with. And I can briefly state all the points that were agreed upon and I can explain them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Before you do that, sir, is this a document that you would have received at the time? We see that it's dated 27th February 1997. You need to speak your answer just so that it can be recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: We did receive this document in Pristina a day or two after the 27th, so we received it either the 28th of February or on the 1st of March, depending on how many days there were in February of that year. So this is a note from this working meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, we see that the document refers to the initiation of an investigation of the leader of the group, Lahi Brahimaj, and it refers to measures and activities that are going to be taken. Based on the information you have -- had at the time, do you know why it was decided by the RDB to conduct an investigation into Lahi Brahimaj and his activities?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: That last question does rather sound as if it's either calling for speculation or calling for the witness to express an opinion; or alternatively leading, and it's objectionable on all three grounds in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Why do you think it's speculation? What I see here is: Based on the information you have had at the time, do you know why it was decided by the RDB to conduct an investigation into Lahi Brahimaj and his activities? No, or not speculation. The question is: Do you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, as long as it's confined to answering that precise question, then I don't object. But I'm just putting down a marker, shall we say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I suggest we only -- we don't put markers, Mr. Harvey. We object when an objectionable statement is made. Yes, Madam Kravetz, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think the question is perfectly okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could you please go ahead and answer my question, sir.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I do know and the State Security Service at that time knew that in 1995 and 1996 there was a series of terrorist actions carried out, attacks at police and citizens at houses in that area, in the Klina, Decani, and Djakovica triangle of municipalities. And the information acquired by this operations section of the RDB in Djakovica indicated that this was a group headed by Lahi Brahimaj. So the meeting was on that topic and specific activities were agreed at at the meeting, the most important of which would be to -- initial processing which would be part of the Krug, or circle, action headed by the RDB in Kosovo and Metohija against Albanian terrorism to give the priority in their work to the persons from the said group headed by Brahimaj and through him and by processing him to deal further with all of those activities. In that sense --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, you are seen getting up while the witness is talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't seek to interrupt the witness, but he is giving a very long answer which starts clearly demonstrating the dangerous area in which we are embarked because he says at 87, line 6: "And the information acquired by this operations section of the RDB ... indicated ..." Your Honour, at this point, it is quite clear in my submission that we are embarked on levels of primary, secondary, who knows, tertiary hearsay. And it's at this stage, Your Honours, I would respectfully submit what we need is an indication from this witness of what sources of information he was relying on that he is speaking of here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Shouldn't we give Madam Kravetz to do that and see whether she does get to the sources?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, when I see an answer going on for some 20 lines, I begin to worry that we're just straying too far away from the question. But I will listen attentively and try not to interrupt more than necessary. I will not lay down further markers. I think it's very clear where we are going.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harvey. Your consideration is appreciated. You may proceed, Madam Kravetz. Do try to control your witness also. You had asked a very simple question: Do you know? The answer should have been: Yes, I do or no, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm guided.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, just going back to your answer you referred to the information acquired by this operation sector of the RDB in Djakovica indicated that this group was headed by Lahi Brahimaj. Could you just clarify for us and very -- try to be as brief as possible in your answer, to which information you're referring to. What was the source of this information?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: The source of our information in that period were conversations with sources with whom the State Security Service was in touch with. These are live sources, informants, and this is information that we acquired relating to attacks from the police. So this is information on the basis of which the Djakovica RDB sector located, identified Lahi Brahimaj as the leader of a group, as the most extremist person in that area; and that is precisely why he was placed as the focus of this initial processing, through whom all the other actions in that area would be viewed. All the attacks and everything that happened in that area during 1995 and 1996 - and there were numerous attacks - were reported to us by urgent dispatches, informing us about the attacks, the consequences of which were wounding; attacks on houses, killings. And this was the basis on which the decision to hold the meeting in this area was based. So these activities resulted in a meeting that sought to reach specific measures in order to continue action in order to prevent any further such acts from occurring.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, Ms. Kravetz tried nobly to try to ask the witness to be as brief as possible. Your Honours have seen the result. It appears to me that the next question has got to be about those sources because at this stage we are still dealing with hearsay upon hearsay as it appears from the transcript to date. I just draw everyone's attention to the fact that we are a long way from anything that this witness can actually say he knows. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you have any comments to make?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, I'm going to go back to the answer Mr. Harvey made -- Mr. Stijovic made, but I don't think this is the moment to be making submissions on the reliability of the evidence this witness is giving; that is a matter for Your Honours at a later stage when the time comes to assess all the evidence and decide on the weight. So this witness is just responding on the basis of the knowledge he had at the time. That's how I would understand his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I would interpose a thought as well as an objection, Your Honour, which is the witness is not answering the questions as posed. The witness is going beyond answering the question posed. And I would ask Your Honour direct Ms. Kravetz once again to control her witness so that we are not subjected to multiple unsourced hearsay which is something that we raised at the very beginning of these proceedings as being a matter of concern.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: As I understand this witness - and I'm sorry I have to say this because I've been trying to restrain myself from saying this - it looks like this man is in the security department of sorts. He has told us that he was given information by informants. Obviously what we can expect is to be told what he did about that information and tell us what he himself found out after he had received that information. This is how police, I understand, work. They work with informants, they ask people questions, and then they go and investigate. I don't know whether this is the direction that is going to be taken, but -- and I was trying to stay away from saying this, but I do think that for a witness of -- of who holds the position that this gentleman held at the time, this kind of source is accepted, provided he tell us what he did. And what this Chamber is going to look at is what he himself did as a result of that information and what he found out on his own.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That may well be the case, but once again as I have said repeatedly, we should not be putting the cart before the horse. Whether or not he did in fact rely on informants and did in fact receive information from that is a different issue. Did you get information, yes or no? I mean, we're -- basic examination. Who, what, when, where, how.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Kravetz, who, what, when, where, how.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I do wish to point out that some of the issues my learned colleagues are raising were already addressed in the prior testimony of this witness and I'm trying to avoid going into all the same detail again. He has in the past already spoken about the sources of his information, and since we're proceeding under 92 ter it may seem a bit disjointed because he's not providing -- going into all the detail again at this stage --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's a question of control, Madam --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- you know, this is the problem and I've found in this Tribunal people get asked what's your question: What's your name? And then we get the whole history about the family tree of that person instead of just being told what my name is. And, you know, I think it becomes important for counsel to be alive to that kind of problem and to try and control his or her witness. You know, listen to your question, ask the question, listen to the answer, get the answer, and stop the witness. Because you control that discussion, you know what -- where you want to go; he doesn't know where you want to go. So you are -- you should lead him. That's why it's a leading examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, just going briefly back to the document, we see that what is stated in this official note is that the group led by Lahi Brahimaj will be observed and investigated and future measures and activities aimed at this group have been agreed. Very briefly, do you know which measures were taken by the RDB at the time to observe and investigate the activities of this group?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could you tell us what those were?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Besides the regular measures, to infiltrate our informants among the ranks of that group, we also used measures of secret wire-tapping of telephone conversations of the family telephone of the Brahimaj family. We also did covert surveillance of Mr. Brahimaj and we co-ordinated and synchronised all the information that we received regarding the activity of the persons in that territory or throughout the whole area of Kosovo and Metohija in co-ordination with the service that was working in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You referred to a covert surveillance of Mr. Brahimaj. Could you explain what you meant by that.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Covert surveillance and monitoring is a special measure applied by the State Security Service. It is conducted by staff of the RDB, and they physically monitor the contacts of the person depending on the requirements and the needs of the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did this surveillance of Mr. Brahimaj and also the other measures you've referred to there, the wire-tapping, et cetera, did that continue into 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but in 1998 we had a problem to carry out the covert surveillance because Brahimaj did not go to Djakovica and Pec so often. He evaded doing that, so it was very limited, the opportunities to apply that measure. So we mostly relied on informant information and information that we gleaned from wire-tapping the Brahimaj family telephone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me ask you a question, Madam Kravetz. I thought this is a 92 ter witness. How long are you still going to be with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I only have five documents for him, Your Honour, so this is one and I have four and I'm moving away. I just have one more question in relation to this document and I'm moving away from it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, we see in this document - this is the first paragraph or second paragraph actually - where it says -- it refers to Lahi Brahimaj as being the leader of the group in Jablanica. Based on this surveillance and operation and investigation you conducted also into 1998, are you able to tell us whether he remained the leader of the group based in Jablanica also in 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this document into evidence, 03 -- 03067 [sic].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, for clarification, when counsel requested the document it was 65 ter 03069 and not 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have 7, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: In that case, 03067 is Exhibit P124. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we just move to the next document, that is 03068, 65 ter 03068. And again, if the B/C/S version could be displayed for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You have the document, sir, before you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Very briefly, sir, could you tell us if you're familiar with this document and tell us, if you are, what it is.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I am familiar with the document. This is an official note of the state security department Djakovica dated 21 September 1997. In this note there is a short account for the high -- for the senior officers of the service in Pristina, saying that a raid on Jablanica is planned. The note was drafted based on information that we received earlier by means of an urgent telegram from Djakovica. And in this document the leadership of the Djakovica department is assessing the current situation in that area, and they are passing on information, stating that the operation would be premature at that moment. That the plans of the police had been uncovered and that the group members in Jablanica were aware of the preparations for that action. The higher leadership is asked to --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: -- refrain from launching that action --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If I may stop you there. We see in paragraph 4 of this document, it refers to the fact that the Djakovica RDB is investigating the same group, it says illegal enemy group in Jablanica. Is this -- in the Lahi Brahimaj investigation, is this the same investigation that we saw referred to in the previous document or is this a different investigation that's being referred to here?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: It is the same investigation. It's the result of a working meeting that took place in February in Djakovica in the state security centre department and it's mentioned in the document I have spoken about.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wish to tender this exhibit into evidence. It's 03068.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 03068 will be Exhibit P125.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could we now please have 03014 up on the screen and I would like page 4. And if we could have only the Albanian displayed for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, we see here a document that is entitled: UCK issues statement on the execution of collaborators" and it refers to in paragraph 1 to two ethnic Albanians accused of collaborate with authorities in Belgrade being executed by the Kosovo Liberation Army, the ethnic Albanian group said in a statement on Wednesday. Do you see that, sir, the first paragraph. I see you nodding, sir, so I'll move on. If you move further down in the document it refers to two persons Jakup Kastrati, the local LDK chief and his deputy Cen Desku, who were arrested by the KLA military police because they were called on people to surrender their arms incorporated with collaborationists, the KLA statement said. Sir, we see that this is dated 4th November, 1998. Did your service have information at the time about this specific -- oh, I think we have the wrong -- I'm sorry, I see why you're looking puzzled. We have the wrong page on the screen. Yes, I see why you're --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: This is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes. We'll deal with the page on the screen, sir, and we'll turn later to the other page. I see where you were. So page 4 which is on the screen is entitled: "UCK claims responsibility for killing Albanian SPS member." And we see the first sentence refers to an ethnic Albanian Maliq Sheholli was shot dead by an unknown gunmen in Podujevo last Thursday evening, Serbian press reports said the next day. The Serbian press singled out the fact that he was a member of the SPS, and the only man of Albanian ethnicity on the SPS list." Did you have any information at the time about this attack? We see that this is dated 13 January 1997.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could you tell us what sort of information you had at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Since November or December 1996, we had information that in the area of Podujevo a group was active that was led by Zahir Pajaziti [Realtime transcript read in error "Bajaziti"] also known as Wolf, a person who initiated the actions of the first major KLA group in that area. By surveillance of his activity or monitoring of his activity we obtained information that the person killed Maliq Sheholli himself. I knew Maliq Sheholli personally, I also knew his family. He was an employee of a firm in Podujevo and he was -- he had some media presence because he was a member of the Socialist Party of Serbia. What is being shown to me here is a translation of a text that was published in some Albanian language publication. It would have been Koha or some other daily.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And if we look at the middle of the page -- of this page it says that: "An alleged Albanian organisation calling itself the UCK, the Liberation Army of Kosova, has claimed responsibility of killing of Maliq Sheholli through a fax message dated 12 January ..." and it doesn't give a date but it's 1997. Sir, is the information you had at the time about this incident consistent with what is stated here in the document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: This statement by the KLA was made post festum. We did have information about the killing of Maliq Sheholli and Inspector Milos Nikolic, who was killed in his village which was done in the immediate vicinity of Podujevo. And we knew that this was done by a group headed by Zahir Pajaziti. Later, that is in late January of the following year, after another action in which Pajaziti took part, tried to arrest him, but after an exchange of fire near Vucitrn a member of our special forces was wounded and Zahir Pajaziti was killed. Another man by the name of Hoxha and his cousin, Hakim Zejnulla [phoen]. I can add that we were tapping the phone that was in the house where Zahir Pajaziti stayed illegally in a neighbourhood of Pristina and we had him under covert surveillance. On that day when he got killed, we tried to arrest him at the bus station in Pristina, but he noticed the people who were following him and he was able to abscond.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Just a clarification, you -- the transcript records the name as "Zahir Bajaziti". Is that the correct name of the person you were speaking about?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: No, it is Zahir Pajaziti, P like Paris, so it's Pajaziti.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Could we turn to page 6 of this exhibit. And if, again, only the Albanian could be displayed for the witness -- I'm sorry. I would like page 5 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So, sir, this is the page that I was referring to earlier. It says the -- it's entitled: "UCK issues statement on 'execution' of collaborators." And it's dated 4th of November, 1998. I'll give you a moment to look at it. It refers to two ethnic Albanians accused of collaborating with authorities in Belgrade being executed by the Kosovo Liberation Army. And towards the bottom of this article it refers to two persons, Jakup Kastrati, the local LDK chief and his deputy Cen Desku being arrested by the KLA because they were called to surrender arms to the Serbian authorities and co-operate with collaborationists the KLA statement said. Sir, how does this information in this press report about members of the LDK being targeted by the KLA accord with the information your service had at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, may we just establish what "at the time" means. Does this time mean several months after the end of the indictment period or does it mean some other time?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I was -- I was going to establish that with the witness. I'm asking specifically of the time of the document with -- which is November 1998 and I was going to move to the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, if you can say "November 1998," that would be very helpful, Madam Kravetz. Okay, it's November 1998. That's the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is merely one in a series of events that happened in the previous period, that is, in 1998. The target of which were not only members of the LDK, the Democratic Alliance of Kosovo, but also members of other ethnic Albanian political parties who advocated a more moderate approach to the solution to the problems prevailing in Kosovo at the time. And we had abundant information about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm having a problem with my headphones. That's why I'm pausing after each answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you need the technician's assistance?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: No, there's some problem, but I think I'll survive for the next five minutes left of the hearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, you referred to the previous period, you said "that is 1998." Are you speaking about the entire year? Are you speaking about a specific period in 1998 where you had heard about these attacks? If you could just specify.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I will try to be as precise as possible. The State Security Service, since 1996 through 1997 and 1998 registered such activities as this. So this was nothing new. If necessary, I can provide examples that will be very telling.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So if I understand your answer correctly, you're not only referring to 1998 but the period prior to that as well? Is that what you meant to say in your answer?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And very briefly, sir, what is the source of your information, that members of the LDK were being targeted by the KLA during this period that you've referred to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Specifically interviews with the members of those political parties that were active in Kosovo and Metohija and the information that we received from our informants and the information obtained through surveillance. And there is a large amount of information of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Based on the information that you were able to obtain at the time, do you know why it is that members of the LDK were being targeted by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I would need a couple of minutes just to explain the context that prevailed at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Stijovic. The question is: Do you know? You don't need a couple of minutes to do so. Yes, you know; or no, you don't know. Then she will ask you the next question if she wants you to explain. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Just to clarify my question is: Do you know why it is that these attacks happened against members of the LDK?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the answer is going to be: Yes, I do know why; or no, I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do know why.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And could you tell the Court how it is that you know this and ...

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: I personally spoke to the president of an ethnic Albanian political party who in the month of August was arrested together with members of some other political parties in the area of Drenica after the anti-terrorist operation carried out by the police and the army. That is one example where we reconstructed in a very detailed fashion the activities that were being taken then.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Going back to my question, I asked you if you knew why and you said: Yes, I do know why. So why is it -- I'm sorry, I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, just this, he said in the month of August. He didn't say what year.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, could you clarify when you say "in the month of August" which year you were referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now going back to my question - and it's almost the end of the session so I'll ask you to be very brief on this - do you know why it is that these attacks happened? You said "yes," so why is it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN STIJOVIC
utterances.text: The gist in one sentence is the difference in approach to resolving the problem in Kosovo and Metohija. The Democratic Alliance of Kosovo and other Albanian political parties like the Democratic Christian and the Social Democratic parties were for negotiations, for dialogue. The KLA were against that and they insisted on resolving the problem by means of an armed conflict and through weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I see we've run out of time. I have a couple more questions in relation to this document. I can resume tomorrow morning and then I will just have one additional document to show to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I think just for the clarity of the record maybe we should have the -- this document be admitted at this stage and I can take it from where we left off today tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Basis?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: On the first basis the incidents that are being discussed are outside the indictment period both before and after the indictment period. The second basis being that as I understand the state of the documents that we have before us at the present time, what we have is an Albanian translation of a copy of a document in English from the northern -- North European Service, although as -- when I look at the document itself there seems so have been -- the source of the news report itself seems to be from Pristina, Yugoslavia. So I think there's some difficulties just in terms of the authenticity of the information that's been presented to the Court with regard to the translations. Also, and in addition, at this point in time we have only had discussion with regards to pages 4 and 5 of this document. So I'm not entirely clear as to what the Prosecution wishes to have go into evidence because the document itself is more than that -- consists of more pages than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If I can address that, Your Honour. I'm only seeking to tender into evidence the two pages that I've shown to the witness, that is, pages 4 and 5 of this exhibit, which is 65 ter 03014. In relation to the objections raised by my learned colleagues, I wish to draw to your attention the fact that documents of the exact same type are already part of the trial record in this case, they have already been admitted into evidence by this Trial Chamber, and this is on the basis of a joint motion filed by the Defence and the Prosecution in the case. And I'm referring specifically to P65, which is a witness statement of a witness called Jakup Krasniqi. If Your Honours look at page 14 of this witness statement, this is annex 2 of the witness statement, a document of the exact same type that I'm currently discussing with the witness is attached and forms part of that exhibit and this is dated -- this is a KLA communiqué dated 3rd -- 8 August 1997. So it is prior to indictment period. Page 90 of the same exhibit is another annex, annex 19, and it's a communiqué of 17th October 1998, and it's also outside of the indictment period. These documents form part of this witness statement which my learned colleagues from the Defence agreed to have admitted in this case as part of the trial record. So this -- these type of documents are already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And that indeed is true and it was testimony from the trial in which the specific witness authenticated the communiqués.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm at a loss and I would like guidance specifically from you, Madam Kravetz. Maybe the Defence might also have. At the beginning of your examination of this witness you tendered his statement and you tendered annexes to his statement. Defence didn't object to you tendering them en masse. Do I understand that this document that is on the screen is not part of those statements, that's why you seek separate tendering of this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour's understanding is correct. These are additional documents. We had indicated in our 92 ter application that one of the reasons we were seeking to call this witness as a 92 ter witness was to elicit additional evidence on certain new exhibits and the Defence had been notified of which exhibits we intend to use during this examination. So that's why I'm proceeding and tendering document by document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: These are not part of the associated exhibits for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. That clarifies me because I was already wondering whether -- is it a viva voce witness or is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And only so that the record is complete with regard to my objection, the documents that the Prosecution presently seeks to tender are reports from daily newspapers concerning what they believe to be or what they are reporting are communiqués from the KLA. So it's actually even, once again, a step removed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. It's a step removed. But the problem I have is that the Rules of this Tribunal allow hearsay evidence and where do you make -- draw the cut-off?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Where do I draw the cut-off?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Cut-off line.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, I draw the cut-off line I think probably at a point which is a bit more conservative than others do; however, I don't believe that the use of wholesale hearsay which is something that I have discussed with you before is appropriate. And I leave it in your fine hands, independent of what the Rules are here at the Tribunal as regards hearsay. There is a certain not only qualitative issue that exists with regard to hearsay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: -- in terms of admissibility not in terms of weight. If it's garbage in, there's no reason to take it. There's no reason to burden your minds with garbage. And if it's multiple, unsourced hearsay or multiple hearsay that you're going to have to plough through and ultimately make an admissibility determination about which has been what the conversation has always been, I suggest to you don't need to do that. In your wisdom and in your thoughts you can say from the outset you can say we're not in interested in having this quality of evidence presented to us because it doesn't assist us in the fact-finding process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: It's unreliable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In my wisdom, I will admit it into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 03014 will be Exhibit P126 and, Your Honours, if counsel can notify Registry when those pages are uploaded in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: We will do that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you so much. Is that then the end of your examination for the day?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: For the day, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just add although the document has been admitted and there was no disagreement last time, my learned friend from the Prosecution is right, there was substantial submissions made about the weight to be attached and those will be highlighted in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: I'm simply adding that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. We will stand adjourned to tomorrow, 9.00 in the morning in the same courtroom. Court adjourned.
